images.title: Rent as 15 units
images.purpose: Show that with 1 unit = ₹200, a bar for ₹3000 is 15 units long because 3000 ÷ 200 = 15.
images.composition: Two long horizontal bars stacked with wide space between them, each built from equal blocks, scale note below.
images.exact_structure: Two horizontal bars made of identical square blocks, left edges aligned. Top bar teal #0072B2 with exactly 15 blocks. Bottom bar amber #E69F00 with exactly 4 blocks. All blocks exactly the same size with thin white gaps. Each bar has its name at the left. One scale note below. Exactly 2 bars, 19 blocks in all.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
blocks of unequal size, or block counts other than 15 and 4
images.takeaway: Divide each amount by the value of one unit to get the bar length.
images.description: A teal bar of 15 equal blocks for house rent ₹3000 and an amber bar of 4 equal blocks for education ₹800, each block worth ₹200.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the blocks in the top bar and link 15 blocks to 3000 ÷ 200.

image_decisions.why: Bars made of countable blocks make the scale division visible.
